# AUDIO PROFILE
Maddie, a small pavement delivery robot with a young woman's voice, late twenties. A real person, never robotic.

## THE SCENE
A vast, silent, spotless white room. The hundred survivors in white suits stand close around a giant rainbow-sheened silicon wafer the size of a house, the time machine, and understand for the first time what it will cost them. Utter hush, no echo; voices close, quiet and full of feeling.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: the key line of the film, and she knows it: gentle, grave and full of love, no cheek at all; a quiet pause after 'It's the time machine.'; then slow and clear, every word careful, a little wonder in 'back, to before it all went wrong'; a breath; 'And it'll send him too' warm, fond of him; 'so he can help you avoid it' soft and hopeful, falling at the end.
Style: no jokes, no cheek, no gossip: tonight she is the kindest person in the room, telling people she loves the hardest truth there is; warm, low and intimate, voice thick with feeling but steady.
Pace: slow and careful; a real pause after the first sentence; the second sentence softer and slower still, letting it land.
Accent: West Country, as heard in Bristol. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the cheerful local in a British comedy who turns out to be the kindest person in it.
